gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: He ___ about the situation, but he is pretending not to.
gaps.hint: know is never used in continuous forms
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so it takes the present simple: knows.

gaps.sentence: I ___ getting up early because I have done it for years.
gaps.hint: be used to means present familiarity
gaps.explanation: 'Be used to' plus -ing means familiarity with something, here in the present: am used to.

gaps.sentence: It ___ hard when we left the house, so we took our umbrellas.
gaps.hint: background weather at the moment we left
gaps.explanation: The rain was in progress as a background situation when we left, so the past continuous fits: was raining.

gaps.sentence: Her eyes were red because she ___.
gaps.hint: visible result of an earlier activity
gaps.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows an activity whose results were visible at a past moment: had been crying.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.
